roster.known_issue: Its own diagnostic flagged this before it was scored, and the result is consistent with it. The Page recursion assumes mean-zero increments under the null, but a merchant's cross-sectional RANK is persistent: a consistently high-risk merchant sits near the top of its cohort every day and the accumulator ramps without anything having changed. A smoke run put 15.4% of merchant-days at the cap with alert_jaccard_wow 1.000. `accumulator_frac_at_cap` is written onto every result row so this is checkable rather than narrated. Run as pre-registered and NOT tuned.
roster.name: rank_cusum
roster.note: The one new SCORING rung of cycle 4, and the only rung on the ladder whose objective IS detection delay rather than a classification score with latency inherited as a side effect. It could not have been evaluated before cycle 4: detection_rate_d7 was 0.000 for a perfect oracle on cycle-3 data. Declared CUTTABLE FIRST in the pre-registration's cut order — the cycle's findings do not depend on it. INSEPARABLE was pre-declared as a likely and acceptable outcome, because the realised validation latency denominator is 7 merchants and carries a standard error near 20pp.
roster.result: Scored on cycle-4 validation, 5 seeds, both exposure arms. Best precision@K on the whole ladder (0.9132, arm B) and best calibration (ECE 0.0061). But the rung built to optimise detection delay does NOT have the best detection delay: Rung 2, plain LightGBM on windowed aggregates, beats it 0.0862 to 0.0831 on detection_rate_d30. Mechanism gate (median alert_jaccard_wow in [0.30, 0.85]) passes on arm A at 0.3490 and FAILS on arm B at 0.2783. p99 scoring latency is unmeasured, not passed - its cost is a per-day cross-sectional ranking and a blend fit, not a per-merchant call. LIMITATIONS.md 9.6.
roster.title: Page/CUSUM on the within-day cross-sectional rank of the incumbent score
